subject.title: [Bug]: Clarify Telegram channel_post auth when groups[chatId].allowFrom is configured

question: For Telegram channel_post commands, should configured groups[chatId].allowFrom be ignored in favor of explicit channel chat allow, or should channel_post fail closed when sender-scoped authorization is configured?
rationale: This is an authorization boundary on a Telegram update type whose native command path does not currently have a normal human sender identity, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security semantics.

options.title: Fail Closed When Sender Auth Is Configured
options.body: Treat sender-scoped per-chat allowFrom as unsupported for channel_post commands and return or document a clear denial until a stronger identity model exists.

options.title: Allow Explicit Chat Only
options.body: Permit channel_post commands from explicitly configured channel chats and document that sender-scoped allowFrom is intentionally ignored on this surface.

options.title: Fold Into Bot-To-Bot Policy
options.body: Defer this narrow rule until broader Telegram bot-to-bot policy work defines peer-bot and channel identity semantics together.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed When Sender Auth Is Configured
recommendation.body: Treat sender-scoped per-chat allowFrom as unsupported for channel_post commands and return or document a clear denial until a stronger identity model exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The native command auth history is the closest current-main ownership signal for the command authorization behavior that needs the policy decision.
